title: Private Capital-Markets & Order Management Platform
subtitle: Full-stack workspace UX, i18n, notifications, and back-office fee configuration on a microservice trading stack.
description: Shipped full-stack workspace and onboarding improvements on a private microservice trading platform, measured by 30 merged commits across Vue workspace modules and Spring OMS APIs, by implementing client scoping, i18n, notification UX, and back-office fee configuration end-to-end.

contribution.label: Full-Stack Contributor (Senior-Reviewed)
contribution.headline: Targeted full-stack slices across Vue 3 workspace modules and Spring Boot OMS back-office endpoints within a senior-led microservice team.
scope: Workspace UX, client scoping, and i18n refinements across the Vue 3 / Quasar frontend
Authentication surface and notification UX updates
Back-office (BO) fee configuration UI and matching oms-service API endpoints
Architecture discussion, proposals, and peer review with full-stack leads (Sazal & Shamim)

problem.statement: High-density trading and back-office workflows require consistent client scoping, localized UI surfaces, reliable notification delivery, and synchronized fee configuration between the web workspace and backend OMS services.

improvements.before: Fee configuration lacked synchronized end-to-end UI and OMS service endpoints
improvements.after: Unified BO fee configuration flow spanning boAccount UI and oms-service APIs
improvements.how: Implemented boAccount workspace views and matching Spring Boot OMS endpoints

improvements.before: Inconsistent client scoping, localization gaps, and fragmented notification UX
improvements.after: Consistent client scoping, localized UI copy, and streamlined notification handling
improvements.how: Refined Vue 3 / Quasar workspace, auth, and notifications modules

myImpact.label: Cross-Repo Delivery
myImpact.detail: 24 frontend commits and 6 backend commits merged Nov 12–16, 2026

myImpact.label: Frontend Modules
myImpact.detail: workspace, auth, notifications, and boAccount flows in Vue 3 / Quasar

myImpact.label: Backend OMS Slice

product.summary: A private multi-service capital-markets and order-management platform built with a Vue 3 / Quasar / Capacitor client and a Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.3 microservice backend behind Spring Cloud Gateway.

architectureSummary: Web and mobile clients (Vue 3, Quasar, Capacitor) route through Spring Cloud Gateway to domain microservices—including OMS, CAT, market data, and exchange adapter services—backed by PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ.

keyDecisions.challenge: Synchronizing back-office fee configuration between the workspace UI and OMS domain rules
keyDecisions.decision: Implemented end-to-end BO fee configuration across the boAccount frontend module and matching oms-service API endpoints under senior-reviewed architecture guidelines.
keyDecisions.outcome: Consistent fee configuration flow spanning UI validation and backend persistence.

keyDecisions.challenge: Maintaining clean workspace scoping, localization, and notification clarity across user roles
keyDecisions.decision: Delivered targeted refinements in workspace, auth, and notifications modules without disrupting established platform conventions.
keyDecisions.outcome: Cleaner dealer/investor workspace flows and localized UI messaging.

securityReliability: Client details, tenant hosts, and proprietary workflows omitted under NDA
